newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: World's most valuable stamp sold for $2.26 mln.
newsitem.headline: World's most valuable stamp sold for $2.26 mln.

text.p: The world's most valuable single postage stamp, a flimsy Swedish issue from 1857, was sold at a public auction on Friday for 2.87 million Swiss francs ($2.26 million dollars), a world record.

The stamp, known to collectors around the globe as the "Treskilling Yellow", had an estimated price of up to $1,2 million. It was purchased for an unnamed private client by a stamp dealer based in Stockholm.
"I am very proud to have the honour to purchase the most valuable item in the world," the dealer, Hans Lernestal, told reporters. He said it was bought for a client but declined to give his name.

The stamp, alreay hailed in the Guinness Book of World Records as the most valuable object of any type by weight, volume and density, had been owned by many of the world's top collectors since it first went on the market in 1885.

It was last sold in 1990 for $1,2 million, also by Geneva-based Irish philatelic auctioneer David Feldman who conducted Friday's sale at a Zurich hotel. "Over two million is incredible," Feldman told Reuters afterwards.

Bidding started at 900,000 Swiss francs ($708,661) and was over within two minutes when Lernestal took his offer to 2,5 million Swiss francs -- to which 15 per cent commission is added to make up the final sum to be paid.
